title: Slaughterhouse-Five
events_chronological: Billy Pilgrim is born in Ilium and grows into a weak, peculiar child.
Billy's father throws him into the deep end of a swimming pool to teach him to swim, and Billy sinks to the bottom.
Billy is drafted as a chaplain's assistant and sent to Europe with no training worth the name.
Billy is lost behind the lines with a scout called Roland Weary, who beats him for wanting to be left to die.
The two are captured, and Weary dies of gangrene on the prison train, blaming Billy with his last breath.
Billy is held in a camp with British officers who have been receiving double rations for years through a clerical error.
Billy is sent on to Dresden and housed with other prisoners in a disused abattoir.
Dresden is destroyed by fire in a single night, and the prisoners in the meat locker come up to find the city gone.
Billy and the others are made to dig bodies out of the cellars until one of the diggers dies of the dry heaves.
Paul Lazzaro, a fellow prisoner, promises to have Billy killed one day on Weary's account.
Billy comes home, collapses, and is hospitalised, where a patient introduces him to the novels of Kilgore Trout.
Billy marries Valencia, the daughter of the optometry school's owner, and becomes a rich man.
Billy survives an air crash in Vermont, and Valencia dies of carbon monoxide poisoning driving to the hospital.
Billy is taken by Tralfamadorians and kept in a zoo on their planet with the film star Montana Wildhack.
The Tralfamadorians explain that all moments exist at once and that free will is an idea peculiar to Earth.
Billy goes on a radio talk show and tries to tell the world about the aliens and the fourth dimension.
Billy's daughter Barbara decides he is senile and takes over his affairs.
Billy is shot dead by a laser gun after addressing a crowd, exactly as he has always known he would be.
syuzhet_notes: The narration jumps without warning between the war, the marriage, the alien zoo and the death, often mid-paragraph and often several times a page. It is not a frame with flashbacks and not two alternating strands; the sequence is associative and the book says as much.
fabula_notes: The chronology is fully recoverable from ages, ranks and the fixed date of the firestorm, even though the telling refuses to lay it out.
